ms.q: Which findings characterize the physical activity transition from adolescence into young adulthood? (Select all that apply)
opts: Self-reported activity declines by an average of ~5 min/day (49 studies)
Accelerometer-measured activity declines by an average of ~7.5 min/day (9 studies)
Both men and women experience reductions in daily physical activity
Total activity decline is slightly larger in males due to higher adolescent baseline activity
ms.rationale: Meta-analyses confirm longitudinal declines in activity during young adulthood (~5 min/day self-report, ~7.5 min/day accelerometer) in both sexes, with larger absolute drops in males.

ms.q: Which adult health conditions are linked to low cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2peak) and physical inactivity during adolescence? (Select all that apply)
opts: Cardiovascular morbidity and premature mortality
Metabolic syndrome and insulin resistance
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Acute epiphyseal growth plate expansion
ms.rationale: Low adolescent VO2peak and inactivity are established independent risk factors for adult cardiovascular disease, metabolic syndrome, type 2 diabetes, and mortality.

ms.q: Why do teenage boys display higher relative VO2peak (60 mL/kg/min) than teenage girls (49 mL/kg/min)? (Select all that apply)
opts: Higher circulating testosterone during pubertal development driving muscle mass growth
Lower average percentage body fat in males compared to females
Higher hemoglobin concentration in males supporting blood oxygen carrying capacity
Complete absence of functional mitochondria in female skeletal muscle
ms.rationale: Sex differences in relative VO2peak stem from higher male testosterone (greater muscle mass), lower male essential fat, and higher male hemoglobin concentrations.

tf.q: In the Young-HUNT Study, mean relative VO2peak was 60 mL/kg/min in teenage boys and 49 mL/kg/min in teenage girls.
tf.feedback: True. Maximal treadmill testing established normative relative VO2peak averages of 60 mL/kg/min in boys and 49 mL/kg/min in girls.

tf.q: In the Young-HUNT Study, high VO2peak was strongly associated with low resting heart rate in both boys and girls.
tf.feedback: True. High cardiorespiratory fitness was strongly correlated with a lower resting heart rate in both male and female adolescents.

tf.q: Meta-analyses show that daily physical activity increases by 30 minutes per day during the transition into young adulthood.
tf.feedback: False. Meta-analyses demonstrate an objective decline in physical activity during early adulthood (~5 to 7.5 min/day reduction).

tf.q: In the Young-HUNT study, high VO2peak was associated with lower BMI and waist circumference in girls, but not in boys.
tf.feedback: False. High VO2peak was associated with lower BMI and waist circumference exclusively in boys.

cloze.statement: The Young-HUNT Study established normative relative VO2peak values of **60 mL/kg/min** in teenage boys and **49 mL/kg/min** in teenage girls.
cloze.hint: Identify the normative relative VO2peak values for adolescent males and females.

cloze.statement: As youth transition into young adulthood, daily physical activity declines by **5 min/day** in self-report studies and **7.5 min/day** in accelerometer studies.
cloze.hint: Identify the daily activity decline values from self-report and accelerometer meta-analyses.

sa.prompt: Summarize the normative cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2peak) values and key cardiovascular health associations established by the Norwegian Young-HUNT Study in adolescents.
sa.model: The Young-HUNT Study evaluated 570 teenagers aged 13 to 18 years using maximal treadmill testing, establishing mean relative VO2peak values of 60 mL/kg/min in boys and 49 mL/kg/min in girls. Self-reported physical activity correlated positively with VO2peak in both sexes. High VO2peak was strongly associated with low resting heart rate in both boys and girls, indicating superior cardiorespiratory function. However, high VO2peak was significantly associated with lower BMI and reduced waist circumference exclusively in boys.
criteria: State normative VO2peak values (60 mL/kg/min in boys, 49 mL/kg/min in girls).
Identify strong inverse association between VO2peak and resting heart rate in both sexes.
Note that high VO2peak correlated with lower BMI and waist circumference in boys only.

sa.prompt: Describe the longitudinal changes in physical activity that occur during the transition from adolescence to young adulthood, citing meta-analytic evidence and explaining sex differences.
sa.model: Meta-analyses demonstrate a systematic, objective decline in daily physical activity as youth transition into young adulthood. Self-report studies (49 studies) document an average decline of ~5 minutes per day, while accelerometer studies (9 studies) reveal a larger objective decline of ~7.5 minutes per day. While both men and women reduce daily activity during early adulthood, the total absolute decline is slightly larger in males because adolescent boys start from higher baseline activity levels.
criteria: Cite meta-analysis decline figures (~5 min/day self-report, ~7.5 min/day accelerometer).
State that physical activity declines in both men and women during the transition to young adulthood.
Explain that males experience a larger absolute drop because they maintain higher baseline activity during adolescence.
